Only 3 smokes remain, but the reveal uses 4.
The reveal claims the window smoke blocks the ticket-booth AWPer; it does not.
The underpass and rotate-via-mid claims need review by someone who knows the map.
An inferred fact (CT positions) states no basis for the inference.
Evidence matrix is incomplete (does not cover all action x evidence-pair cells).

facts.text: Your team controls top mid after smoking window from T spawn.
A teammate cleared connector with a flash and holds it.
An AWP was spotted at ticket booth ten seconds ago.
Three smokes and four flashes remain across the team.
At least two CTs are on the A side — one stairs, one site.
One minute and five seconds remain in the round.

actions.label: Full A execute with three smokes
Split A through connector and ramp
Continue the default from mid control

qualifiers.label: Smoking stairs, jungle, and CT to isolate the site
Smoking stairs and jungle only, saving one smoke
Leading the entry from ramp with a flash
Sending a player through underpass for a flank

followup.heading: Window smoke fading
followup.stimulus: The window smoke has faded. The AWPer is now visible holding from ticket booth, watching top mid.

updates.text: The AWPer is confirmed at ticket booth, scoped toward top mid.
Window is now open — no smoke cover for mid crossing.

responses.label: Re-smoke window and proceed with the original plan
Execute immediately before the AWP repositions
Abandon mid control and rotate toward B

events.action: The team re-smoked window and executed onto A with three smokes covering stairs, jungle, and CT.
events.consequence: The AWPer was locked behind the window smoke, unable to contribute. The split from connector and ramp overwhelmed the two defenders.
events.state: The bomb was planted on default with forty seconds remaining.

comparison.roundAction: Full A execute with coordinated smokes after re-smoking window.
comparison.materialInformation: The confirmed AWP position at ticket booth and the faded window smoke.
comparison.roundFollowup: Re-smoking window was essential — it neutralised the AWP threat and restored the mid crossing.

debrief.whyItWorks: Three smokes isolate each defensive position on A site. The AWPer behind ticket booth cannot reposition through a window smoke. The split from connector and ramp creates two angles that a two-player defence cannot hold simultaneously.
debrief.cost: All three smokes are spent, leaving no utility for a post-plant retake defence.
debrief.assumption: The A site has exactly two defenders, and the AWPer is locked behind window.
debrief.breaksWhen: If a third CT rotated from B through connector undetected, the flank during the execute would catch the team off guard.

evidenceReview.explanation: The confirmed AWP at ticket booth made re-smoking window decisive — without it, crossing mid was suicide.
Three smokes allowed the full isolation execute. Fewer smokes would have forced a partial smoke that leaves a gap.

debrief.followupReview: Re-smoking window was the strongest response. Rushing without it exposes the mid crossing to the AWP. Rotating to B wastes the mid control advantage.
debrief.strongestAlternative: Executing immediately without re-smoking window. Faster, avoids utility cost, but the AWPer gets a free angle on the mid crossing.

counterfactual.changedFact: If the team had only two smokes remaining instead of three.
counterfactual.effect: The full isolation execute is impossible. A split through connector with only stairs and jungle smoked becomes the best option, accepting the risk from CT spawn.

debrief.method: Synthetic scenario written for Roundcraft as editorial tactical analysis. It is not a recording or reconstruction of a professional match.

reveal.principle: When an AWP position is confirmed and your smoke cover expires, re-smoking is not optional — it is the prerequisite for every other decision.
